newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-L.Lease in A$350 mln Brisbane project.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-L.Lease in A$350 mln Brisbane project.

text.p: Financial services and property group Lend Lease Corp Ltd said on Thursday it and General Property Trust had sought approval for a A$350 million proposal to develop Brisbane's Riverside Centre.

"Lend Lease Development and General Property Trust (GPT) are seeking approval from Brisbane City Council to develop the remainder of Brisbane's popular Riverside Centre with a mix of uses including hotel, residential and office," Lend Lease said.
"Lend Lease Development and GPT, which own the land, have entered into a cooperative agreement for the preparation of the joint development application," Lend Lease said.

"The A$350 million proposal includes a tower south of the existing GPT-owned Riverside office tower which would incorporate a mix of low rise office space and high rise serviced residential apartments."
It would include another tower further to the south which would feature a four star hotel and residential units and a third tower to the north of the existing building.
The project would also have a public river front promenade which would replace the existing temporary bridge linking the Riverside and Waterfront developments.

"A landscaped plaza containing restaurants, cafes and shops would provide direct pedestrian access from the river and ferry terminals to the city via the fig Tree junction in Eagle Street," Lend Lease said.

Lend Lease Development's Queensland management, Des Marks, said the demand projections for residential, hotel and office space in Brisbane indicated it was timely to proceed with the completion of Riverside.
Lend Lease Development is carrying the costs for the preparation of the development application.
The agreement gives GPT the opportunity to participate in the development of the office and serviced residential apartments component at a future date.
It also grants both GPT and Lend Lease Development a right to buy each others lands should one of the two not to proceed with the joint venture.
